:::{#exm-linear-decay}
#### Linear decay between two step lengths

Take $s^{(0)} = 0.1$, $s^{(\schedlen)} = 0.001$ and $\schedlen = 90$.
The [step length](#def-linear-decay) at $t = 0, 45, 90, 120$ is:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: linear-decay-r
#| code-fold: false
s0_ld <- 0.1
sT_ld <- 0.001
tau_ld <- 90
t_ld <- c(0, 45, 90, 120)
frac_ld <- pmin(t_ld / tau_ld, 1)
data.frame(t = t_ld, step_length = (1 - frac_ld) * s0_ld + frac_ld * sT_ld)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: linear-decay-python
#| code-fold: false
s0_ld, sT_ld, tau_ld = 0.1, 0.001, 90
for t_ld in [0, 45, 90, 120]:
    frac_ld = min(t_ld / tau_ld, 1)
    print(t_ld, round((1 - frac_ld) * s0_ld + frac_ld * sT_ld, 6));
```

:::

The step length falls by the same amount at each update,
then stays at $0.001$ after update $\schedlen$.

<!-- no-figure: the example tabulates four step lengths -->

:::
